description:
pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs:196

The default method `check_revocation_against_anchor` returns `crate::Result<()>` but has no `#[must_use]` annotation. The provided default always returns `Ok(())` silently. While this is called via the trait object dispatch path (not directly by callers of the default), Rust convention requires `#[must_use]` on Result-returning trait methods so that an implementor who accidentally omits the override and calls the default in their own code cannot silently drop the result.

More importantly: the trait method `check_revocation` also lacks `#[must_use]`. Both should be annotated.

Fix:
```rust
#[must_use = "revocation check result must not be silently discarded"]
fn check_revocation(&self, cert: &Certificate, issuer: &Certificate) -> crate::Result<()>;

#[must_use = "revocation check result must not be silently discarded"]
fn check_revocation_against_anchor(...) -> crate::Result<()> { Ok(()) }
```

clippy lint: `must_use_candidate` would flag these.
title: Add #[must_use] to RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor default
